Widespread Protests in Panama Disrupt Transit, Trade Amid Political Crisis

PANAMA CITY, June 13—Widespread anti-government protests erupted across Panama this week, blocking major highways and disrupting operations at the strategic Panama Canal, raising concerns about repercussions for global trade flows.

The unrest follows the National Assembly’s approval of emergency austerity measures and a controversial mining reform bill late Monday. Demonstrators, including labor unions and indigenous groups, have set up barricades in Panama City and other key transit points. Authorities said at least 22 major roads remain blocked, slowing domestic logistics and halting some cross-border shipments.

Canal authorities confirmed Thursday that vessel transits through the Panama Canal, which handles about 6% of global maritime trade, were operating at reduced capacity after picketers prevented employees from reaching job sites. “We are working to maintain safe passage for ships, but delays are unavoidable under current conditions,” said Javier Ruiz, spokesperson for the Panama Canal Administration.

The Panamanian Chamber of Trade estimated economic losses from the disruptions at over $50 million since Tuesday. “The situation is critical. Businesses cannot move goods, and exporters are facing mounting backlogs,” said chamber president Elisa Mendoza.

President Luis Navarro urged for calm and dialogue in a televised address, calling on protesters to lift blockades. “Our country’s stability and prosperity depend on resolving our differences peacefully,” Navarro said.

Regional analysts warn that a prolonged crisis could further strain global supply chains already facing pressure from other geopolitical tensions. No timeline for the resolution of the unrest has been announced.
